newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators propose brownfields tax breaks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators propose brownfields tax breaks.

text.p: In a bipartisan effort, Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun, an Illinois Democrat introduced a bill Thursday to provide $2 billion in tax breaks for businesses that clean up and redevelop contaminated, abandoned industrial sites, called "brownfields".

The bill has the support of Republicans Sen. Spencer Abraham or Michigan, Alfonse D'Amato of New York, and james Jeffords of Vermont, as well as the Clinton administration and Senate Minority Leader Thomas Daschle.
President Bill Clinton is expected to include the tax incentive in his budget proposal next week.
The proposal would allow businesses to deduct from their federal income taxes the full cost of cleaning up brownfield sites.

"Nationwide, the initiative would provide a $2 billion tax incentive designed to leverage up to $10 billion in private funds to help pay for the removal of pollutants from some 30,000 urban and rural brownfield sites.

The bill comes on the heels of broader brownfields legislation introduced earlier by the Senate Democratic leadership and provisions by Abraham in a Superfund toxic waste cleanup bill offered by the Republican leadership.
The Democrats are pushing for a standalone brownfields bill, popular among cities and communities, which are eager to create jobs through new commercial development.
